clue.text: Put in prison — about time!

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that a long-overdue criminal has finally been locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To cage someone is to confine them behind bars, as a jail does.

clue.text: Caught American gambler after decoding message

indicators.note: decoding scrambles a word out of its coded order, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
A is a standard abbreviation for American
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A US gambler is arrested once a coded message has been cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: A cablegram is a telegram sent by undersea cable, so it is a kind of message.

clue.text: Grumble after travel bag tore at the back

indicators.note: the final letter is placed following the bag, so one piece comes after the other
the back of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a grip is an old word for a holdall or travel bag
the final letter of tore

explanation.surface: Someone complains because their luggage has split at the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: To gripe is to complain, a colloquial synonym for grumble.

clue.text: Impressive digital snap?

blocks.note: E- is the prefix for electronic or digital things, as in email
a pic is a photograph, a snap

explanation.surface: Praise for a striking photo taken on a digital camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is used informally to mean grand or impressive in scale.

clue.text: Whiff infanta periodically got in her rice dish

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
the selected letters get inside the dish, held within it

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of infanta
paella is the Spanish rice dish; her refers to the Spanish infanta

explanation.surface: A Spanish princess gets a whiff of something in her paella.
explanation.walkthrough: An infanta is a Spanish princess, which is why her dish is paella, the Valencian rice dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiff is an old slang word for a small thin cigar, and a panatella is exactly that kind of cigar.

clue.text: My Dutch master's crazy driving could be the end of him

definitions.text: driving could be the end of him

indicators.note: crazy suggests letters gone wild and out of their sane order

blocks.note: all fourteen letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone fears their Dutch master's wild driving will kill him.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash test dummy is the mannequin put in cars driven into walls, so driving is literally designed to finish it off.

clue.text: "Crazy Mike" — exposed husband who swears a lot

definitions.note: a relative clause; the answer is a noun for such a person

blocks.note: potty is British slang for mad
Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M
something exposed is out in the open
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A man nicknamed Crazy Mike has been outed as a husband with a foul tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A potty-mouth is someone who habitually uses obscene language.

clue.text: Work out question persistently carried by press

indicators.note: the first piece is carried along by the second, which follows it

blocks.note: to pump someone is to keep questioning them for information
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Puzzling over a question the newspapers keep pushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like solve; it is the gym sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump iron is slang for lifting weights, a gym workout.

clue.text: Feeling that is singular, tense, most sensitive?

blocks.note: touch is the sense of feeling
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A grammar-lesson list of terms that ends by wondering which is most sensitive.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchy means easily offended, so the superlative describes the most sensitive person.

clue.text: Oik's exclamation of joy

blocks.note: first meaning: a boorish, uncouth person
second meaning: a whoop of delight

explanation.surface: The whoop let out by a lout.
explanation.walkthrough: An oik is British slang for a crude, ill-mannered person; in Swift the Yahoos are brutish humans.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse lout, and yahoo is also a cry of glee.

clue.text: Conflict across both sides of the sea

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its first and last letters
the conflict stretches across the letters, enclosing them

blocks.note: a war is an armed conflict
the first and last letters of the

explanation.surface: Fighting on both shores of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea is a body of water, so water stands in for it.

clue.text: Subject of proud song woman coined?

blocks.note: first meaning: the figure hailed in the patriotic anthem Rule
second meaning: the seated female figure stamped on British coins

explanation.surface: A riddle asking who a proud anthem is about.
explanation.walkthrough: The helmeted female personification of Britain appeared on the old penny and still on some coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia is the allegorical woman representing Britain, both sung about and minted on coinage.

clue.text: See 6 across
Peak most demanding when taking southern face?

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, removing the face or front letter
'face' keeps only the first letter of 'southern'

blocks.note: the most severe, hardest task is the most demanding
S for southern, which is also the word's face, its first letter

explanation.surface: Climbers ask which peak is hardest when tackled from the south face.
explanation.walkthrough: Everest's south face is a real climbing route, which makes the surface feel like mountaineering.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest mountain peak.

clue.text: Routine dry grass implement advertised on the radio

indicators.note: something advertised on the radio is heard, not seen, so the sounds count

blocks.note: hay is dried grass
a hoe is a garden implement

explanation.surface: A radio ad for hay and a garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Heigh-ho is used as an adjective for something dull and humdrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Heigh-ho is a weary sigh at monotony, so used attributively it means dull and humdrum.

clue.text: See 20
Bother, annoy, nag, ultimately torment Billy's mum

indicators.note: to bother something is to disturb it, so the letters are stirred up
ultimately points to the very end, the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix
taken as written for the mix
the last letter of torment

explanation.surface: A list of ways to pester a little boy's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy looks like a boy's name; it is a billy goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A billy goat is a male goat, and a mother goat is a nanny goat.

clue.text: Drunk left in bed, missing Mass

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so that letter is dropped
the letter for left is placed inside the bed

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
the bottom of a river or sea is its bed
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A drunk is left sleeping it off in bed and misses church.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely intoxicated.

clue.text: See 5
Close game between seeded finalists

indicators.note: the finalists are read as the final letters of each preceding word

blocks.note: the last letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A tight tennis match between two seeded players in the final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close game' reads as a tight match; Close alone is the definition, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of something is its conclusion, its end.

clue.text: Rhondda MP Pat Chambers suppressing evidence of leak

indicators.note: the name is pressed down inside the words, kept out of sight within them

blocks.note: runs from the end of Rhondda into Chambers

explanation.surface: A Welsh member of parliament is accused of covering up a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhondda is a Welsh valley constituency; the political leak in the surface is really a water leak.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet stain on a wall or ceiling is the visible sign that water is getting in.

clue.text: Entire night disturbed, finding at last something to calm baby

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled
at last points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix
the last letter of finding

explanation.surface: Parents endure a sleepless night before finding something to soothe the baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A teething ring is a ring a baby chews to ease sore gums, a soother.

clue.text: Sultanate banishing old fellow

indicators.note: banishing sends something away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: Oman is the Arabian sultanate
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A Gulf state expels an elderly man.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow and man are interchangeable words for a male person.

clue.text: Glide past section of Silverstone (lap 7)

indicators.note: a section is a cut-out part, a run of letters spanning the words that follow

blocks.note: the last letter of Silverstone
taken as written
the first two letters of the figure written out as seven

explanation.surface: A racing car sails past a rival on the seventh lap at Silverstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Silverstone is the British Grand Prix circuit. It works as a hidden word once the figure is written out as a word: the run spans three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse as it slips by, so to elapse is to pass smoothly.

clue.text: Staunch second XI missing ace

indicators.note: missing means going without, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
an eleven is a cricket or football side
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A loyal reserve side plays without its star player.
explanation.walkthrough: Staunch reads as a loyal adjective; here it is the verb meaning stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch bleeding is to stem it, both meaning to check a flow.

clue.text: Impulsive after strong beer? It's a wee problem

indicators.note: after places the word for impulsive following the beer word

blocks.note: nappy is an old word for strong, heady ale
rash means acting without thinking

explanation.surface: Something hasty after strong beer, then a question about a small problem.
explanation.walkthrough: A nappy is the British word for a diaper; wee is both small and urine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nappy rash is skin irritation caused by a wet diaper, so it is a problem caused by wee.

clue.text: Bet Julius, say, made unlimited togs for little 'un

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundaries, so the end letters go

blocks.note: to lay money is to bet it
Julius is the setter of this puzzle

explanation.surface: A wager that the setter will produce endless baby clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Togs is British slang for clothes, and little 'un a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the full set of clothing and bedding prepared for a newborn.

clue.text: Climber set up a fastening device

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a nail fastens things together

explanation.surface: A mountaineer rigs up an anchoring device.
explanation.walkthrough: Climber looks like a mountaineer; it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests.

clue.text: Whiskey unloaded from power boat

indicators.note: unloading takes cargo off, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: Whiskey is the NATO alphabet word for W
weight is power or influence, as in carry weight

explanation.surface: Smuggled whisky is offloaded from a speedboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power boat' reads as one thing; split it into power and boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight is a racing rowing boat crewed by eight oarsmen.

clue.text: Composed principally daft, unrefined, repellent wordplay gag

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or first of all, so the first letter is taken
something repelled is driven back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the first letter of daft
raw materials are unrefined
a pun is a joke that plays on words

explanation.surface: A disgusted verdict on a crude, silly crossword joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A document drawn up has been drafted or composed.

clue.text: New revolutionary song ready for Nigeria

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the song is read backwards

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A rousing new anthem is prepared for the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready looks like prepared; ready is slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is Nigeria's currency, its ready money.

clue.text: Dressing slices of caribou loin

indicators.note: slices are thin pieces cut at intervals, so letters are taken alternately

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A sauce served with sliced reindeer meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise served as a sauce or dressing.

clue.text: Advantage in court?

blocks.note: surface reading: a legal edge in a lawsuit
setter's reading: in tennis, a player on advantage is one rally from taking the game

explanation.walkthrough: Court suggests law, but it is a tennis court, and advantage is the tennis score after deuce.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, advantage means one point away from winning the game, which is the moment called game point.

clue.text: Like special suit for flier — US soldier — retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: a stretch: winged ants fly
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A pilot's special suit and a retreating American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter admitted on the Fifteensquared blog that this wordplay does not work. Reading flier as a flying ant is the nearest fit, with GI reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-g suit protects pilots from blacking out under the high acceleration forces of flight.

clue.text: Starts to take over young sister's playthings

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: An older child grabs their little sister's toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Toys are things children play with, playthings.
